A1.justification: Both PDFs describe DeepResearchGuard and DRSafeBench. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables, and appendices support comparison despite substantial reformatting and relocation of material.

before.justification: v1 reports original safety and report-quality experiments, progressive guard ablations, guard-model comparisons, and reference-quality and runtime measurements.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds GPT-5 evaluations, human ratings, intervention statistics, token measurements, and domain-level results.

M1.justification: The four guards, taxonomies, severity-dependent actions, memory retrieval, planning rules, human overrides, and substantive prompts are retained. Algorithms 1–2 move to Appendix D. Explicit uniform report-score weights and threshold-selection explanations add documentation without establishing a changed procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 828 DRSafeBench queries and 200 stage-wise tests, with unchanged category counts and synthetic threat scenarios. The new examples and eight-domain breakdown describe existing coverage; human ratings assess existing reference and report tasks.

E2.justification: v2 adds GPT-5 to the backbone comparisons. The guard comparison also changes its reported model from GPT-5-mini in v1 Table 5 to GPT-5 in v2 Table 4 while retaining the same scores. The PDFs do not explain whether that change represents replacement or correction of the model label.

E3.justification: Appendix I.5 adds a human-rating protocol using 11 CS Ph.D. students, 30 randomly sampled references, and 30 reports rated on matching 1–5 scales. GPT-5 configurations are also evaluated. The existing metrics, synthetic attack procedures, and deer-flow limits of one planning iteration and three search steps remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained progressive ablation and guard-model comparison, v2 adds analyses of human intervention and disagreement, human-versus-LLM judgments, token consumption by stage, and domain-specific safety performance in Appendices I.4–I.7. These substantially extend scrutiny of evaluator reliability, operating burden, and variation across domains.

E5.justification: Appendix H.3 first reports three full pipeline runs and confidence-distribution percentiles used to select intervention thresholds; it does not establish an increase from a previously specified run count. Existing standard-deviation reporting continues, while v1's runtime coefficient-of-variation discussion is omitted.

E6.justification: v2 adds substantial GPT-5, human-rating, intervention, token-cost, and domain-level results. GPT-5 DSR increases from 47.34% without guarding to 57.36% with guarding. The original four backbones' DSR/ORR rows remain unchanged; the average gain changes from 18.16 to 16.53 percentage points over the expanded model set. DeepSeek-v3 output F1 changes from 0.69 to 0.68 in the corresponding stage-wise tables.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and algorithmic rules retain their substance. The reference-safety formula remains in Appendix C, and newly displayed formulas restate existing definitions. The explicit arithmetic mean for reference quality explains the previously specified average; no new theorem, proof, or formal assumption is introduced.

C1.justification: The framework, benchmark, and first multi-stage safeguard contributions remain. The abstract and conclusion extend the empirical claim to GPT-5 and revise the headline DSR improvement from 18.16% to 16.53%. The abstract also changes the over-refusal claim from a reduction by 6% to reduction to 6%.

C2.justification: v2 substantially expands interpretation through discussion of passive versus active guarding, application-dependent latency trade-offs, possible guard overconfidence, LLM–human rating alignment, and domain robustness. These appear in Appendices A.5 and I.2–I.7. The original limitations concerning novel attacks, confidence, and retrieval dependence are retained and moved into the main document.

D1.justification: v2 newly specifies uniform report-score weights, threshold-selection criteria, reviewer times, and token costs by stage. Existing prompts and execution budgets remain available. However, v1's direct code-repository link is removed, while the appendix's promise of a future repository release remains.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations including ResearchRubrics and Doc-Researcher, removes works including Deep Research Comparator, and more explicitly contrasts integrated guarding with systems such as LlamaGuard and WildGuard. These update supporting context without substantially changing the central research positioning.

P1.justification: The introduction and experimental discussion are extensively rewritten and condensed. Algorithms and the metric catalog move into appendices, limitations move into the main document, and an appendix contents list and explanatory sections are added. The title and author list also change.

P2.justification: The predominantly single-column preprint becomes a two-column document, substantially changing placement and sizing of figures, tables, and pseudocode. Existing plots are largely redisplayed, with updated labels and table highlighting. New tables present domain composition, human ratings, intervention counts, token costs, and domain-level safety results.

improvement.justification: The new human ratings expose LLM-judge optimism, while intervention, token, and domain analyses make reliability and deployment costs more assessable than in v1. These provide a modest net gain in empirical transparency. The improvement is limited by reporting inconsistencies, including 21% human intervention in Appendix I.2 versus 5.4–11.4% in I.4, and removal of the direct repository link.
